strategic_horizon.terminal_goal: Build a personal cross-platform VPN whose logical weak-network behavior approaches UDP/QUIC while public carriers remain stock REALITY/Vision over real kernel TCP.
strategic_horizon.current_milestone: M10-003 real two-lane weak-network and fault-injected QUIC qualification
strategic_horizon.local_optimization_stop_rule: Do not tune RBC/FEC policy, freeze a production FEC frame, modify REALITY/Vision, or start TUN/platform integration until real local fault-path tests validate the deterministic 150-300 ms / 10-20% loss direction. Mandatory profiles include normal 40-60 ms, 150-300 ms jitter with 10% and 20% impairment, correlated burst loss, and at least one worse 250-600 ms / ~30% profile. Keep the 2.0x intentional-redundancy ceiling.

continuation_cursor.last_completed_action: Completed M10-002 at substantive HEAD 29878fc5f5545ab6a73e62491f5aa0e182fc700b: recovered from an interrupted sandbox, qualified the pinned quic-go v0.61.0 oracle locally using a SHA-verified GitHub Actions build relay without upgrading the WBD Go 1.23 module, and added a separate deterministic two-lane stress layer. The exact relay artifact ZIP SHA-256 d3353e3f55fc5abad3e4e5e1b1cdf71e7a0ccb181c3368a69cba497208737e49 and oracle binary SHA-256 9482defb23b556faf0af0f7f48b8108c1e589973c861969d1d9ee750f3e224a1 were verified locally; the binary then completed 64 QUIC STREAM and 64 QUIC DATAGRAM loopback RTT samples with bidirectional DATAGRAM support. Stress profiles now cover normal 40-60 ms/0%, mobile 80-150 ms/2%, 150-300 ms/10% (2 seeds), 150-300 ms/20% (2 seeds), and 250-600 ms/30% (2 seeds). Protection traffic pays an independently sampled alternate-lane propagation/recovery delay, eliminating the earlier unrealistic instant-protection artifact. Final root-module vet, normal/race tests, protocol fuzz (~143,899 executions), Linux/386, Linux/mipsle, Windows/amd64 benchmark cross-builds, wbd-stress cross-builds, handoff verification and continuity tests passed; remote CI/handoff/oracle relay also passed.
continuation_cursor.current_task: M10-003: move the 150-300 ms / 10-20% and worse profiles from deterministic two-lane modeling into real local fault-path tests, and inject controlled faults into the locally qualified QUIC oracle so WBD, TCP, UDP and QUIC can be compared under the same weak-network schedule.
continuation_cursor.why_now: M10-002 proved the QUIC oracle can run locally and showed that deterministic weak-network conclusions vary strongly by seed at 20%+ impairment. The remaining uncertainty is whether those trends survive real kernel socket queues, correlated path impairment and QUIC recovery rather than only independent sampled lane models.
continuation_cursor.done_when: Local sandbox tests exercise at least normal 40-60 ms, 150-300 ms with 10% impairment, 150-300 ms with 20% impairment, a correlated burst-loss case, and one worse 250-600 ms/~30% case through a real fault path or equivalent user-space packet/socket proxy. Native TCP/UDP, WBD 1.5x/2.0x candidates and pinned QUIC STREAM/DATAGRAM are measured with p50/p95/p99/completion, delivery ratio where applicable, intentional bytes, and reproducible seeds. Results explicitly distinguish independent-lane from correlated-loss behavior. If CAP_NET_ADMIN/netem is unavailable, use a deterministic user-space fault proxy and record the limitation rather than substituting Actions results.
continuation_cursor.next_atomic_action: M10-003: build a real localhost two-lane fault proxy with reproducible seeded delay/loss schedules and run normal 40-60 ms plus 150-300 ms/10% and 20% cases first; add correlated burst impairment and 250-600 ms/~30% after the basic proxy is stable. Route the pinned locally qualified QUIC oracle through the same controlled fault path before any M11 RBC tuning.

udp_like_status.current_best_variant: not_selected: normal networks show no protection latency win; 10-30% stress results are seed/path-shape dependent and still need real correlated-fault and QUIC weak-network qualification
